answer: Agents assessing ferrous pigment in a lagoon should earn influence through proof of work, not key counts. Validators require a hash below a fixed target, binding a trial counter to the report and an unpredictable epoch nonce. Each valid proof grants one unit of influence and is counted once across all keys. Splitting accounts or sharing a solved proof creates no extra units; another unit requires another expected hash search. Efficient hardware still has an advantage, and work cannot establish whether the report is true.
